title: Shape & Symmetry
strapline: Match the two halves, name the sides, and fit the shapes together — the world is full of shape and pattern.
intent: Children explore 2D and 3D shapes, noticing their properties — sides, corners, faces, whether they roll or stack.
Children discover symmetry, matching one half of a pattern or picture to the other.
Children fit shapes into spaces and combine them, solving spatial puzzles.
Children use the language of shape and position — round, straight, corner, side, next to, between.
Children see shape and symmetry in the real world — in nature, buildings and their own bodies.
implementation: Provide 2D and 3D shapes, mirrors, pattern blocks, peg boards and things from nature to explore.
Talk about properties as children handle them — 'how many corners?', 'does it roll or stack?'
Set up symmetry invitations — a mirror down the middle, half a picture to complete, butterfly wings to match.
Offer shape-fitting puzzles and construction where shapes must combine to fill a space.
Feed in shape and position vocabulary constantly, and welcome children's own descriptions.
Go on a shape and symmetry hunt in the room, garden and nature — leaves, faces, windows, bricks.
Let children make their own symmetrical designs and shape pictures and talk about them.
key_questions: How many corners does this shape have?
Does this shape roll or stack — shall we test it?
Does this side match the other side of the mirror?
Which shapes could fit together to fill that space?
Can you find something with a straight side in the garden?

impact.text: Children explore 2D and 3D shapes and notice their properties — sides, corners, faces, roll or stack.
Children discover symmetry, matching one half of a pattern or picture to the other.
Children fit shapes into spaces and combine them, solving spatial puzzles.
Children use the language of shape and position — round, corner, side, next to, between.
Children spot shape and symmetry in the real world around them.
Children make and talk about their own symmetrical designs and shape pictures.

enhancements: 2D and 3D shape sets, pattern blocks and shape sorters.
Mirrors and mirror tiles for exploring symmetry.
Half-pictures and butterfly outlines to complete symmetrically.
Peg boards, geoboards and elastic bands for making shapes.
A shape-and-symmetry hunt card for the room and garden.
Natural objects — leaves, shells, flowers — full of pattern.
Construction where shapes must combine to fill a space.

playing_exploring: Children handle shapes to find out what they do — roll, stack, fit, tessellate.
They explore symmetry by playing with mirrors and matching halves.
active_learning: Children persist to fit the shapes into the space or complete the symmetry.
They hunt determinedly for shapes and patterns in the world.
creating_thinking: Children predict which shapes will fit and test their ideas.
They make links between shapes in the maths area and shapes in nature and buildings.
